stem: The three main organs (institutions) of government are the legislature, the judiciary and the:
solution: The three organs of government are the legislature (makes laws), the executive (implements them) and the judiciary (interprets them).

stem: The organ of government that makes laws is the:
solution: The legislature (Parliament at the Union level) is the law-making organ of government.

stem: The Parliament of India consists of the President, the Lok Sabha and the:
solution: Parliament comprises the President, the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).

stem: In money matters, the final say rests with the:
solution: The Lok Sabha exercises supreme power in money matters; once it passes the budget, the Rajya Sabha cannot reject it.

stem: The Council of Ministers is responsible to the:
solution: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha and must retain its majority support.

stem: The Lok Sabha can remove the Council of Ministers by passing a:
solution: If the Lok Sabha passes a no-confidence motion, the Council of Ministers must resign.

stem: The ministers who are elected representatives and take major policy decisions form the:
solution: The political executive (ministers) is elected and takes major policy decisions; the permanent executive (civil servants) implements them.

stem: The permanent officials (civil servants) who assist ministers form the:
solution: The permanent executive (bureaucracy/civil service) consists of officials who assist the political executive and run day-to-day administration.

stem: Why does the political executive have more power than the permanent executive?
options: Because it is accountable to the people and represents their will
Because it is appointed by judges
solution: The political executive has more power because it is elected by and accountable to the people, unlike the appointed permanent executive.

stem: The Prime Minister is appointed by the:
solution: The President appoints as Prime Minister the leader of the majority party or coalition in the Lok Sabha.

stem: The other ministers of the Council of Ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the:
solution: The President appoints the ministers on the advice of the Prime Minister.

stem: The head of the government at the national level is the:
solution: The Prime Minister is the head of the government; the President is the head of state.

stem: The President of India is the:
solution: The President is the head of state and the nominal executive, while the Prime Minister is the real head of government.

stem: The President exercises his/her powers mainly on the advice of the:
solution: The President generally acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.

stem: The President of India is elected by:
options: An electoral college of elected MPs and MLAs
solution: The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college of the elected members of Parliament and the State Legislative Assemblies.

stem: The highest court in India is the:
solution: The Supreme Court is the apex (highest) court of India.

stem: The power of the judiciary to declare a law invalid if it violates the Constitution is called:
solution: Judicial review is the power of the courts to strike down laws or actions that violate the Constitution.

stem: The independence of the judiciary means that it is:
options: Free from the control of the legislature and executive
solution: Judicial independence means the judiciary functions free from the control of the other organs, ensuring impartial justice.

stem: The government decision discussed in the chapter — reservation of jobs for 'backward classes' — was based on the recommendations of the:
solution: The office order reserving 27% of government jobs for socially and educationally backward classes was based on the Mandal Commission's recommendations.

stem: The order implementing reservation for backward classes was challenged and finally decided by the:
solution: The reservation order was challenged in court and its validity was finally settled by the Supreme Court.

stem: This example shows that a major government decision usually involves:
options: The executive, the legislature and, if challenged, the judiciary
solution: A major decision typically involves the executive (which decides), the legislature (which debates/legislates) and the judiciary (if the decision is challenged).

stem: Members of the Lok Sabha are:
solution: Lok Sabha members are directly elected by the people through general elections.

stem: Members of the Rajya Sabha are mainly:
options: Elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies
solution: Most Rajya Sabha members are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies.

stem: The Lok Sabha is generally more powerful than the Rajya Sabha in matters relating to:
options: Money (budget) and the survival of the government
solution: The Lok Sabha is more powerful in money matters and because the Council of Ministers is responsible to it (not the Rajya Sabha).

stem: The Council of Ministers is headed by the:
solution: The Prime Minister heads the Council of Ministers, which forms the political executive.

stem: The Cabinet is:
options: The most powerful group of senior ministers within the Council of Ministers
solution: The Cabinet is the inner, most powerful group of senior ministers within the Council of Ministers, which takes key decisions.

stem: The principle of 'collective responsibility' means that:
options: The whole Council of Ministers is accountable to the Lok Sabha and stands or falls together
Ministers answer only to the President
solution: Collective responsibility means the entire Council of Ministers is jointly accountable to the Lok Sabha.

stem: The separation of powers among the three organs is important because it:
options: Prevents any one organ from becoming too powerful
solution: Separating powers among the legislature, executive and judiciary prevents the concentration and misuse of power.

stem: The judiciary protects citizens' rights through the power of:
options: Judicial review and hearing cases including PILs
solution: The judiciary protects rights by judicial review and by hearing cases, including Public Interest Litigations (PILs).

stem: A key reason for having independent institutions in a democracy is to:
options: Check the misuse of power and ensure decisions follow proper procedure
solution: Independent institutions check the misuse of power and ensure that decisions are taken through proper, lawful procedures.

stem: The formal head of the Indian state, in whose name the government functions, is the:
solution: The government functions in the name of the President, who is the formal (constitutional) head of state.

stem: The presiding officer of the Lok Sabha is the:
solution: The Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha, conducting its proceedings and maintaining order.

stem: The power to interpret the Constitution and the laws rests with the:
solution: The judiciary has the power to interpret the Constitution and the laws.

stem: The 'political executive' is preferred over 'experts' for major decisions because:
options: Elected representatives are accountable to and represent the people
solution: Major decisions rest with the political executive because elected representatives, unlike experts, are accountable to and represent the will of the people.

stem: The Supreme Court and the High Courts can be approached by citizens to:
solution: Citizens can approach the Supreme Court and High Courts to enforce their Fundamental Rights.

stem: Institutions sometimes cause delays and disagreements, but they are necessary because they:
options: Ensure decisions are properly considered and power is not misused
solution: Though institutions can slow things down, they ensure decisions are carefully considered and that power is exercised responsibly.

stem: The government's proposals for taxes and expenditure (the budget) must be approved by the:
solution: The budget — the government's taxation and spending plan — must be approved by Parliament, with the Lok Sabha having the final say.

stem: An independent judiciary can even declare a decision of the government or a law of the legislature:
solution: Through judicial review, an independent judiciary can declare a law or government action unconstitutional and invalid.

stem: The Prime Minister remains in office as long as he/she:
options: Commands the support of a majority in the Lok Sabha
solution: The Prime Minister stays in office only while commanding the support of a majority in the Lok Sabha.

stem: The three organs of government are designed to:
options: Work together while checking and balancing one another
solution: The three organs work together while also checking and balancing one another to prevent the misuse of power.

stem: Which of the following correctly pairs an institution with its role?
solution: Parliament makes laws, the executive implements them, and the judiciary interprets them.

stem: The office memorandum on reservations shows how the __________ takes and implements a decision.
solution: The office memorandum illustrates how the executive (the government) takes a decision and issues orders to implement it.

stem: The role of institutions in a democracy is to ensure that decisions are made:
options: Through proper procedures with checks on power
solution: Institutions ensure that decisions are made through proper procedures, with checks that prevent the arbitrary use of power.

stem: Which institution ensures that the government does not misuse its power against citizens' rights?
solution: The independent judiciary ensures the government does not misuse power against citizens' rights, through judicial review and enforcement of rights.

stem: The debate and discussion in Parliament before a law is passed helps to:
options: Consider different viewpoints and improve the law
solution: Parliamentary debate lets representatives of different views examine and improve a proposed law before it is passed.

stem: The permanent executive (civil servants) are expected to be:
options: Neutral and to implement the decisions of the political executive
solution: Civil servants are expected to be politically neutral and to implement the policies decided by the political executive.

stem: The Council of Ministers together with the Prime Minister forms the:
solution: The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers together form the political executive at the Union level.

stem: A well-functioning democracy needs its institutions to be:
options: Weak and controlled by one person
solution: A healthy democracy needs strong, independent and accountable institutions that check and balance each other.

stem: The relationship among the legislature, executive and judiciary is one of:
options: Cooperation along with mutual checks and balances
solution: The three organs cooperate to run the government while also checking and balancing one another.

stem: The overall theme of 'Working of Institutions' is that:
options: Democratic decisions are made through institutions — legislature, executive and judiciary — that share and check power
solution: The chapter explains how the legislature, executive and judiciary together take and implement decisions, sharing and checking power in a democracy.
